subject: Finova evaluation recap, recommended models & acceptance gates
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@finova.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Finova evaluation recap, recommended models & acceptance gates

Hi Samantha — great to meet yesterday. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery focused on model fit and acceptance criteria. TL;DR: we ran the initial prompt set you shared through a trio of candidate open models + your proprietary baseline; attached is the prompt set plus a short benchmark summary and a draft MAP (mutual action plan).

What we observed from the 300-sample pilot:
- Proprietary baseline (Finova-prop-v1): strong at structured extraction but higher latency and a few hallucination cases on policy language.
- Open candidates: Llama-2-Chat-13B (q4_0) balanced cost/latency; Mistral-Instruct-7B showed stronger concise responses on summaries; Orca-30B-mix had best semantic accuracy but >2x cost.

Recommended immediate experiment (3-week):
1) Run a 10k prompt-run on two variants: Finova-prop-v1 (baseline) and Llama-2-Chat-13B q4_0 (open).
2) Evaluate on the attached prompt_set_v1 with the acceptance gates below.
3) If parity is achieved vs baseline on quality metrics, transition to a staged rollout with Redwood routing that preserves your latency SLOs and falls back to the proprietary model for edge cases.

Proposed acceptance gates (draft):
- Intent classification accuracy >= 92% (on labeled subset).
- Extraction precision >= 95% on key-value fields.
- Hallucination rate <= 2% as measured by the hallucination checklist in the prompt set.
- Median token latency under 350ms under target QPS.

Attachments: finova_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (prompt/test cases), finova_benchmark_summary.csv (pilot runs), finova_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft MAP).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm the MAP owners and timeline (column in the MAP).
- We spin up the 10k-sample job and provide a reproducible benchmark report (3 business days after sign-off).
- Neha to propose run config and quantization profile for the Llama variant.

Tagging Neha and Aditya for the config + commercial notes.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.ai]

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova evaluation recap, recommended models & acceptance gates

Thanks Jordan — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the MAP: 
1) For the hallucination metric, is that measured at the token level or response level? We care about business-impacting hallucinations (anything that would cause a regulatory exception).
2) On latency: our production SLA is 250ms median for single-turn prompts. You propose 350ms — is that because of the q4 quantization tradeoffs?

Also can you call out any prompt fixes you applied in the pilot vs our raw prompts? There were a few examples we flagged as adversarial.

If those two points look good we can share the MAP owners and sign-off timeline by Monday.

— Samantha
Senior Product Manager, Finova
Samantha.Lee@finova.com

Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Finova evaluation recap, recommended models & acceptance gates

Samantha — great questions. Answers and a bit more color (quoting the pilot summary):

On hallucination metric:
- We measure hallucination at the response level for this evaluation (binary: business-impacting hallucination flagged or not). For the benchmark CSV we included a per-response tag and a short rationale column so you can audit easily. The gate (= 2%) refers to proportion of responses in the sample that are flagged as business-impacting. If you prefer token-level scoring we can run both; response-level is typically more aligned with regulatory risk.

On latency and the 350ms target:
- 350ms median was the pilot median for Llama-2-Chat-13B q4_0 at your pilot QPS (~8qps) on our Dedicated config. The 250ms in your SLA is tight — two options: (A) choose a smaller model/optimization (Mistral-7B q4f) to hit 250ms with slightly lower semantic accuracy, or (B) keep Llama-13B and use Redwood routing + prefix-KV caching for hot prompts to target 250ms median in staged rollout. Neha: I recommend we include a small bucket of hot prompts in the MAP to validate prefix cache effectiveness.

Prompt fixes applied in pilot:
- Normalized role tokens (system/user), removed ambiguous follow-ups, and added a strict extraction anchor in 12 test cases. All modifications are documented in prompt_set_v1 with comments. We did NOT change any core business rules — just formatting and guardrail tokens.

Recommended model matrix for the 10k-run (what we'll submit to benchmarking):
- Baseline: Finova-prop-v1 (your internal baseline).
- Candidate A: Llama-2-Chat-13B (q4_0) — cost-efficient mid accuracy.
- Candidate B: Mistral-Instruct-7B (q4f) — lower latency, good for short-form tasks.
- Candidate C: Orca-30B (bf16) — higher quality, higher cost (use as a contrast case).

Acceptance thresholds (final draft for MAP):
- Intent accuracy >= 92% (macro-averaged over core intents).
- Field extraction precision >= 95% / recall >= 90%.
- Business-impact hallucination <= 2% (response-level).
- Median token latency <= 300ms for candidate models in production-like config (we can use 250ms target for hot-prompt set once prefix caching validated).

I attached an updated MAP with owners/actions and a sample run config for Neha. If that looks good we can schedule the 10k run for Wednesday (3 business day turnaround), and we'll post the full reproducible report to the Drive link in related_links.

— Jordan

Jordan — this all looks reasonable. We discussed internally and we'll: 
- Confirm MAP owners by EOD Wednesday.
- Greenlight the 10k run (please schedule for Thursday as you suggested).
- If the open candidate reaches parity on the gates you listed, we'll open procurement for a pilot Dedicated pool and proceed to a canary rollout.

A couple of asks before the run:
- Please include a short regression test harness that checks a 50-edge-case subset (we'll provide a list).
- Can you add an explicit 'fallback' rule in the MAP to route to Finova-prop-v1 whenever extraction confidence < 0.6?

Attachment: I uploaded a short list of 50 edge cases to the Drive link you provided.

Thanks and excited to move forward.

Best,
